measurements.note: n=200, d=3, Σd=600. Single shuffle + paired walk; ~33x faster than VL on the same fixture (VL=634540 ns) because no MCMC, no per-window connectivity recheck.
n=600, d=3, Σd=1_800. ~3.86x time for 3x n — close to linear scaling in Σd. Sorted-Vec adjacency dedup adds the log factor.
n=1200, d=3, Σd=3_600. ~2.89x time for 2x n. Versus VL=11522000 ns at the same size, fast-heur is ~54x faster.

n=200, Σd=600, top-heavy (4 vertices d=10, 168 d=3, 28 d=2). Collision rate is higher than the regular case but still single-attempt; cost per collision is sorted-Vec O(log d) plus a residual-bump. ~21x faster than VL on the same fixture (VL=478760 ns).

n=200, Σout=Σin=800. Directed branch maintains two stub bags + per-source sorted-Vec out-arc adjacency. Roughly ~3.7x slower per attempt than the equivalent undirected case (3-regular n=200) due to the doubled stub count and the separate in/out residual tracking.

cross_reference.note: C upstream wraps the same routine in igraph_degree_sequence_game(IGRAPH_DEGSEQ_FAST_HEUR_SIMPLE). Our SplitMix64 RNG path is not bitwise-portable to igraph C / NumPy / R, so absolute medians here characterise the Rust implementation only.

interpretation.primary_cost: Fisher-Yates shuffle over the Σd-sized stub bag + pair walk with O(log Δ) edge-existence test per pair. Restart-from-scratch on infeasibility is rare for graphical inputs and capped at MAX_OUTER_ATTEMPTS=1024.
interpretation.rust_advantages: No MCMC, no allocation inside the pair-walk loop, sorted-Vec adjacency keeps the dedup constant tight. Versus the VL sibling generator (ALGO-GN-025) the fast-heuristic gives 21-54x speedup at the cost of dropping the connectivity guarantee.
interpretation.future_optimisations: 1) Trade the sorted-Vec adjacency for a small open-addressing HashSet at large Δ to drop the log factor. 2) Bias the shuffle toward stubs with the largest residual to lower collision rate on power-law-tailed inputs. 3) On restart, keep the bottom k% of accepted pairs to amortise progress instead of full reset.
